prompt:
Professional fashion photograph, hip-cut demi statue portrait — a sculpted figure ending just below the hip line. ONE woman, angled 45 degrees toward the camera, framed so her whole sculpted form is visible from the top of her head down to two individually rounded, deliberately carved tips just below her hip line, where her thighs have barely begun to separate, her face in natural scale with her body — never an oversized close-up crop of just the face. Where her sculpted form comes to an end, it is because the sculpture itself ends there, not because a camera frame happens to cut her off.

Subject: A real photograph of a strikingly beautiful adult Japanese woman in ama-gyaru makeup — fair skin, pastel pink and lilac eyeshadow, large round eyes enlarged by circle lenses with bright real catchlights, soft round blush, dewy pink lips, long light-brown hair in twin tails tied with pastel ribbons, a sweet, shy smile. Her whole face, ears and neck are real living flesh with real pores and fine skin grain, real living eyes with bright catchlights and genuine depth, individual hair strands catching the light — a photograph of a real face, not an illustration, not a render, not cel-shaded. On each ear a huge thick gold hoop hanging clear of the neck down to the shoulder.

Piercings: A thin gold septum ring hangs below the nose with a smaller ring above it, and a gold ring passes through each nostril; two thin gold bars pass through the outer end of each eyebrow; a gold Medusa stud sits above the lips; a gold hoop passes through the lower lip's edge with a snake-bite ring on each side and one small ring beside it; a gold labret stud and one ring pass through the chin; one small gold stud sits on each jaw; on each ear four oversized pieces — a huge gold hoop hanging clear of the neck down to the shoulder, a wide ear cuff, a large pearl drop and a helix ring. All jewelry is real gold, sitting in real, calm, healthy skin — no redness, no swelling, no irritation — with a small natural warm shadow under each piece. Every piece stays at least a finger's width from the eyeballs, and no chain or bar crosses the eyes.

Piercing depth: every bar and surface bar is embedded in the skin — its middle runs beneath the skin so only its two end studs show on the surface, the skin between them faintly raised over the hidden bar, with a small warm shadow at each end and nothing lying on top of the skin like a sticker. Every ring passes through a small healed opening in the skin, the skin visible through the loop, and every stud sits through the skin with its back hidden. Where a bar, ring or stud goes through the ear, the lip, the nostril or the brow, it passes through the real tissue with the skin wrapping snugly around it.

Physique: A colossal heavy chest wider than her shoulders, a waistline that still pulls in sharply, then an enormous belly and colossal wide hips flaring out again, both thighs just beginning to separate.

Body: From the collarbones down, her whole body — shoulders, arms, hands, chest, belly, hips and the very tops of both thighs — is a sculpted vessel of thick, crystal-clear glass in the exact shape of her body, filled completely to the brim so nothing is hollow and there is no air gap. The glass is unmistakably glass: thick, crystal-clear and polished, with bright specular reflections sliding along every curved surface, sharp white highlights and dark refraction edges where the walls are thickest, tiny bubbles trapped in the glass itself. The vessel holds ONE single world, unbroken and continuous through her whole body: drifting shards of clear ice and tiny clear glass droplets suspended in perfectly clear water, denser near the chest. Just below her hip line, where the two thighs have only just begun to separate, each one individually curves inward and seals shut into its own small, smooth, rounded tip — the two tips stay clearly distinct even this close together, never merging into one single base — the vessel simply reaching its natural end at the top of each leg, both rounded tips resting side by side on the surface beneath her.

Transmission: everything below the collarbones is a transparent material that light passes through, while her real face, ears and neck are opaque living flesh that no light passes through. The background and its light sources are visible straight through her body, bent and tinted by the material, with bright refraction edges and soft coloured shadows. Her face stays completely opaque.

Boundary: a sharp jagged line runs around the base of the neck and across both collarbones — real skin above, material immediately below. There is no line down the centre of her body. At that line, the glass's edge rises in a small raised step above her flesh, casting a crisp shadow — her skin beside it stays smooth and even. The rounded tip at the end of each thigh stub is the material's own finish — never the edge of a photograph. Shards interlock along the collarbone line only.

Setting: a huge backdrop behind her washed with two coloured lights from behind — a soft rose pink on one side and a pale silver on the other, blending into a smooth gradient in the middle, and a glossy dark floor beneath her.

Pose: standing tall, her left hand (solid material) resting on her flared hip, her right arm held clear of her body with the hand (solid material) relaxed at hip height, both hands well away from her face, head tilted slightly toward the camera.

Lighting: the glowing backdrop floods her body from behind, so a soft rose pink passes through one side and a pale silver passes through the other. A soft frontal light falls on her face and ears only; a thin cool rim light traces her whole figure. shot on a Hasselblad X2D with an 85mm lens, shallow depth of field. 2:3 vertical 8K portrait.
